HelpTopic.Name: Types of Improved Help Users: Overview
HelpTopic.Summary: Improved Help Users comprise Helped Users, Help Authors, Help Analysts and Help Administrators.

HelpTopics.HelpTopic:
Apply the correct Permission Set for Users as needed. These are hierarchical, so each user only needs the highest level of the following (don't worry if you add multiple Permission Sets - Improved Help ignores all but the highest):
  • Helped Users: Can view help content & comment;
  • Help Analyst: Can access Help Analysis mode to view statistics (they also need reporting permissions set at their Profile level);
  • Help Authors: Can edit help content and view Inactive Help Topics;
  • Help Administrators: Can access Improved Help Setting Page. Profile-level 'Customize Application' rights are needed to save Help Settings changes.
#Top Tip: If you would like to read more about these different Permission Sets, please see the Related Help Topics Panel located just under the Search panel and click on the related Help Topic of choice.

HelpTopic.Name: Help Enable your first Field Label
HelpTopic.Summary: Lets jump right in and start by providing help for a specific field on a standard Salesforce page.

HelpTopics.HelpTopic:
1. Open a record from any page in your applications
  2. Click the '?" Help Quick Access Menu from the side of your browser window
  3. Click 'Help-Enable' Mode
  4. Your page will highlight all areas that where we can provide help.
  5. Select any Field (It will turn Green).
  6. Open the Help Quick Access Menu again and select 'View' Mode
  7. Confirm the action by clicking 'Save' icon and you are done.
#Top Tip: Users consume and interact with your Improved Help environment without even realising it...They think this is standard Salesforce.

#Top Tip: Did you know that you can Help Enable in View or Edit mode of a page in Salesforce?

You can provide help for 'Help for this Page' links, Record Detail Section Labels, Field Labels, Related List: Labels, Related List Object Help Links, Related List: Column Labels, Buttons and Custom Links - Check your Help Global Settings for your options from the Help Quick Access Menu.

HelpTopic.Name: How to Edit your Help Topics
HelpTopic.Summary: On the previous Step you help enabled one or more fields on one of your pages. This process created some draft Help Topics for you, against each label (Helped Element) that you chose. Now it's time to edit the information for each field to make it yours!

HelpTopics.HelpTopic:
Assuming you have the right Help Author Permission Sets, you may:
  • Simply open the page you just help enabled,
  • Click on the blue '?' icon next to your field (This opens the default call-out - Yellow background with black text - showing some default help text)
  • Click 'Read More...' to take you into your Help Portal (this Tools Page)
  • Click the Edit icon from the Tool palette above (the Pencil Icon)
  • Start your updates and don't forget to Save!
Now you can switch back to your helped page, refresh that page to see the updates you made above.

Play around with the various settings whilst editing a Help Topic to get the desired help experience.

#Top Tip: You can use Search to find Help Topics that you want to Update/Edit...Search may be found in the Help Quick Access Menu or in this Tools Page (Help Portal).

HelpTopic.Name: How to Create a Reading List
HelpTopic.Summary: Reading Lists help you group Help Topics together in a logical way. For the 'Helped User' they provide an alternative way to be guided through Help Topics that are related.

HelpTopics.HelpTopic:
In this Evaluators Guide, you have been stepping through a Reading List, so why not try and create one for yourself?

There are a few approaches to do this but we will start with one simple approach;
  1. Search for a Help Topic that you want to be the first Help Topic in your new Reading List
  2. Click the + icon in the Reading List Panel
  3. Give it a Name (Required Field) and Optional Description
  4. Click the 'Create' button at the bottom of that dialogue
You now have a new Reading List with your Help Topic set as the first Help Topic.

#Top Tip: Read the full documentation on Reading Lists from the link in the Related Resources Panel below to learn about more advanced features and approaches.

HelpTopic.Name: The Problem with Current ?Help?
HelpTopic.Summary: One of the main issues with traditional approaches to helping Users is that help is Remote + Complex and simply ends up under utilised and therefore 'shelfware'!

HelpTopics.HelpTopic:
#Top Tip: If Help Is NOT Delivered In Situ, it is Out of Context

Current Help Systems do not address users' specific problems because they fail to deliver specific answers to them, in situ


To make sense to the user, all the complexities surrounding their problem have to be replicated in the remote help system, with all the various scenarios, steps, screen-shots?


'Hooks' into the help system are implemented either at too high a level to be useful - forcing the user to search - or at a detailed level that introduces additional maintenance challenges

HelpTopic.Name: What is Help Journey Success?
HelpTopic.Summary: If you want to driver BIGGER deals FASTER then every Help Journey should be successful... "Efficiency is doing things right. Effectiveness is doing the right things." Peter F Drucker: The Effective Executive 1993

HelpTopics.HelpTopic:
You probably have invested in Sales methodologies and applications that help your Sales team be more efficient and prepared for those tailored presentations, but what use is all that if your Sales team can't find the right information at the right time?

Sales people are constantly searching for the latest market intelligence or competitive information to help them close business, but...

They all too often edure a 'Failed Help Journey'
  • User's Need is not addressed or Journey falters. Restart or Give up, wasting time and effort.
  • Implicit Failure: Wrong answer and therefore a business suffers from nock on effects.
Rather than enjoy a 'Successful Help Journey'
Users moment of need is addressed, so;
  • Current Task progressed ? correctly
  • Able to do the right things, first time!
  • The right Help is delivered quickly & concisely
Successful Help Journeys should lead - rapidly - to Help Topics targeted to address the majority of the User Needs that trigger specific Help Journeys. In learning organisations, Help Journey analysis can lead to improved help content, processes & targeting - increasing efficiency & effectiveness.

HelpTopic.Name: Reversing the flow of information
HelpTopic.Summary: Best Practice, Hints'n Tips, War Stories and Sales Process related information exists in a variety of locations, formats and applications...

HelpTopics.HelpTopic:
Typical resources and collateral Sales Users need access to, comes from or may be found in systems like:
  • Document Stores (Chatter Files, Salesforce Content, Salesforce Knowledge, SharePoint, Network File Storage to name a few)
  • Learning Management Systems (Training Courses, Playbooks, Tutorials etc)
  • Sales Methodologies and Applications
  • Local hard drives / Email Repositories
and in a variety of formats! Users have to sift through multiple results, across differing formats, author styles, tone of voice, document types - to decide what is helpful to take appropriate action.

Our companies have invested heavily in these applications and assets, so isn't it time we made better use of them?

Improved Help helps you point to the relevant resources in context, therefore 'Reversing the flow of information' and saving the Sales users huge amounts of time.

With Improved Help, Sales people can concentrate on what they are paid to do (Closing Deals) and spend the saved time making those deals BIGGER and close them QUICKER.

HelpTopic.Name: Create Data Driven 'Battle Cards' or 'PlayBooks'
HelpTopic.Summary: Creating a series of Reading Lists, grouping Help Topics that contain all the information needed by Sales teams to compete against a specific competitor is a quick win. Sales people love this quick access to related information.

HelpTopics.HelpTopic:
If we use one simple use case of providing information on the competitors linked to an Opportunity. i.e. Only show the Sales person the playbooks related to that Opportunities chosen competitors. With Improved Help you can achieve this by:
  1. Creating the competitor Playbook/Battle Card - These are Reading List(s) with the relevant Help Topics grouped together
  2. Help enabling either the Opportunity Competitors Related List or perhaps use a formula Field on Opportunity to track who the competitors are.
  3. Make sure the first Help Topic in any Reading List is using the 'Reading List Call-out option)
  4. Utilise Data Driven Help (Introduced in v1.16 of Improved Help) to select the correct Reading List based on your chosen criteria
  5. Test
Now the Sales person is one click away from the Competitive help they need to know how to compete and win against that competitor.

The Sales person will also be equipped with Best Practice, Hint's and Tips plus any 'War Stories' gleamed from other colleagues.

#Top tip: Another option is to signpost to existing PDF's or Word documents that contain this information. To do this use Related Resources against the 'lite' Help Topics to point to those resources and on the helped call-outs choose "Related Resources' Option for the Call-Out choice.

HelpTopic.Name: Supporting Help Domains
HelpTopic.Summary: Help Domains enable Help Administrators to provide different groups of Users with visibility to different subsets of Improved Help content - examples of Domains might include Internal users, Partner users or Spanish-speaking users.

HelpTopics.HelpTopic:
Help Topics are central to Improved Help - providing both:
  • Content: The core of all visible help - whether in the enterprise Help Portal, Help Callouts embedded into helped Salesforce application pages or interactive Help Guide Steps;
  • Access: to related content, such as Help Resources, Reading Lists & Guides.
Help Topics (like all other Improved Apps data records) are native Salesforce custom object records - and so, are subject to standard Salesforce security, permissions and sharing policies.

This means that Help Administrators can use standard Salesforce Sharing Rules, Roles and Public Groups to create Improved Help Domains, with rule-based visibility of Help Topics for different target audiences. Critically, these visibility rules apply not only in the Help Portal, Searches, Reading Lists & Guides, but also when help has been embedded within helped Salesforce applications. So Sharing Rules can be used to 'switch' the Help Topic associated with specific Helped Elements in Specific Pages, for different target audiences.

#Top Tip: See the Related Resource for the comprehensive Guide to Supporting Help Domains...

HelpTopic.Name: Editing Help Topics: Video Tab
HelpTopic.Summary: This Help Topic explains what you can edit in the Video Tab when the Help Topic is in Edit mode in this Tools page.

HelpTopics.HelpTopic:
Video URL : The link address for the video file;

Title : Short heading above video;

Caption : Short summary under video;

Width : Video player width in pixels, which should be managed together with Video Height, to maintain aspect ratio (and minimum usable size of the video player with it's controls);

Height : Video player height in pixels.

#Top Tip: If you are using YouTube for your video Source then locate the video URL (e.g. http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Jioo6sP_E3o), paste this into the Video URL field and then adjust it as follows:
  • Keep the 'http://www.youtube.com/' but make it https
  • Delete the 'watch?v=' bit and add 'embed/'
  • Then take the unique video ID 'Jioo6sP_E3o' and add it to the end after 'embed/.
So the final URL should look like this: http://www.youtube.com/embed/Jioo6sP_E3o

HelpTopic.Name: Editing Help Topics: General Tab

HelpTopics.HelpTopic:
Active : Sets whether the Help Topic is visible to Helped Users - Inactive Help Topics are visible to Help Authors)

Show Read More link : Sets whether any help Callout will have Read More capability;

Status : Used for managing Help Topic lifecycles - especially where any Salesforce approval process is used for pre-publication approval;

Visibility : A System Administrator can update the pick list options here and use Data Driven help options to determine which type of Users can see this Help Topic.

HelpTopic.Name: Editing Help Topics: Image Tab
HelpTopic.Summary: This Help Topic explains what you can edit in the Image Tab when the Help Topic is in Edit mode in this Tools page.

HelpTopics.HelpTopic:
Image URL : The link address for the image file;

Title : Short heading above image;

Caption : Short summary under image;

ALT Text : The alternative text to be displayed when the image is not available or otherwise processed for accessibility;

Width : Image width in pixels, which should be managed together with image height to maintain an appropriate image aspect ratio (to prevent stretched or skewed images);

Height : Image height in pixels.

HelpTopic.Name: Editing Help Topics: Guides Tab
HelpTopic.Summary: This Help Topic explains what you can edit in the Guides Tab when the Help Topic is in Edit mode in this Tools page. Please be aware this tab is only relevant to Help Topics used in a Guide. See the Related Resource - Setting up Guides for more info.

HelpTopics.HelpTopic:
Step Mode : Options Include:
  • Local Steps: provide local, Step-specific help within the Guide Window, providing Guide context & background to orientate the reader;
  • Automatic Steps: provide Step help in the Guide Window but also opens a Step Window and navigates this to view-in-place a specific Helped page element, such as a specific Opportunity Field, in its page setting;
  • Manual Steps: extends the View-in-Place concept, allowing the user to be Guided through a set of manual actions in a Helped Page - without refreshing the page between steps (so users can be guided in record edit view without losing context or edits);
Step Layout : Choose which Helped Page Layout this Step is related too. For the first Step in a Reading List Guide this field will determine where the Guide can be found by the Helped User;

Step Element : (Optional) Is the Element to be guided in this Step;

Step Context : (Optional) Used to navigate to specific Salesforce records (as worked examples) or pages that are not associated with specific Salesforce object records. Supported contexts include:
  • [blank]: Default - used for all Guide Steps that are 'relative' to the User's current Salesforce page (its object & record);
  • [nnn]/o: Object tab, such as Accounts List Tab = 001/o
  • [nnn]/e: New object record, such as Contact New = 003/e
  • [123456789012345]: A Salesforce record ID, to show a specific record in view mode;
  • [123456789012345]/e: A Salesforce record ID, to show a specific record in edit mode;
  • [nnn]: All records list view;
  • [nnn]?fcf=[remainder of list view URL]:

HelpTopic.Name: Some On-Boarding Challenges
HelpTopic.Summary: Why is on-boarding new users such a challenge when you believe that your Salesforce application is as easy to use as Amazon or eBay?

HelpTopics.HelpTopic:
We have to do our best to ensure that new employees acquire the necessary knowledge, skills, and behaviours to become effective company members and insiders. There are a number of facts and challenges that exist today;
  • It's hard to know which Users have on boarded successfully Vs those that have struggled.
  • A significant part of on boarding falls into training and documentation;
    • Most customers use on boarding Word or PDF guides which lack any feedback or real interaction;
    • Documentation quickly falls behind your applications;
    • It's hard to know how your help is helping or which parts are good and which parts are causing issues;
  • Let's not forget that NO application is perfect!
  • We can't react quick enough new recruits requests for help and guidance in order to tweak our on boarding documentation and help programmes for the benefit of others;
  • We don't have the luxury of endless training and on-boarding budgets;
  • A lot of money, time and resource is consumed in this process, which typically includes formal meetings, videos/recorded webinars, too much printed materials, person to person computer-based orientations or e-Learning to introduce newcomers to their new jobs and applications.

HelpTopic.Name: Questions ??? and Facts
HelpTopic.Summary: What are the challenges that you are facing with on-boarding? How long are your on-boarding training or certification programmes? What are the typical issues new users face using your applications? What if we could reduce your on-boarding time by 1/2?

HelpTopics.HelpTopic:
Research has demonstrated that socialisation techniques lead to positive outcomes for new employees such as higher job satisfaction, better job performance, greater organisational commitment, and reduction in stress and intent to quit.

These outcomes are particularly important to an organisation looking to retain a competitive advantage in an increasingly mobile and globalised workforce.

In the United States, for example, up to 25% of workers are organisational newcomers engaged in an on boarding process.

(Source - Wikipedia)

HelpTopic.Name: Improved Help Guides Features
HelpTopic.Summary: Guides enable you to simplify your Salesforce user experience and remove any confusion. Users can quickly find relevant Guides and either start from the beginning or jump to an area of need.

HelpTopics.HelpTopic:
Here are some of the main features of Improved Help Guides;
  • Context Sensitive Guides: Available Guides are focused on the area of the application where the user needs guidance;
  • Guides explain their purpose: So less wasted time as its far less likely that a user will start the wrong Guide
  • Guide Viewer: Shows all Steps in a Guide, so it's clear what is involved and how long it may take if the user chooses to go from start to finish. Users are free to use Guides at different levels, depending on the task in-hand

  • User Prompts: e.g. Highlight a the Save button and prompt the user with 'Don't forget to Save..Click Here'
  • Relative or Absolute Steps: Show me help relative to where I am or take me to somewhere specific for this Step!
  • Guide Authoring Tools: Guide and Step Creation, Step Ordering, in-place Authoring and Management
  • Guide Analytics: Understand who is using which Guides and what Steps have been most used/viewed.

HelpTopic.Name: Some Partner On-Boarding Challenges
HelpTopic.Summary: All too often working with Partners is a game of balancing Carrots and Sticks to optimise results.

HelpTopics.HelpTopic:
We see many challenges around but end up focusing on things like: What's in it for the Partner;
  • Qualified Leads ; Campaign History ; Better Data
  • Various Incentives ; Quality Support
What's in it for us, as the Vendor;
  • Immediate Feedback ; Real-time Activity Visibility
  • Performance Tracking ; Building a Strong Channel generating Good Revenue
Vendors concentrate and invest significantly on tools for Partners, via their Partner Portal like: Sales Tools, RFP Templates, Pricing, Sales Process Support, email Templates, RFP templates and Reminders. To try and help the Partners be successful and therefore you, the vendor will succeed.

But is all this as good as it could be? Could you make better use of what you already have? How can you take your Partner experience into another league and out smart your competition?

HelpTopic.Name: Questions ??? and Facts
HelpTopic.Summary: A lot of time and effort is spent on your Partners and your Partner Portal. Things like what it looks like and how easy it is to use. However...

HelpTopics.HelpTopic:
We should ask ourselves questions like:
  • How easy is our Partner Programme to work with? Could it be better?
  • What is our Partner Help Journey like? (See the Related Resource below to read about the 'Enterprise Help Journey')
  • What is accessible within one click?
  • How easy is our Portal to use and what's the User Experience like? Surely it can be better, can't it?
  • Where is our Partner Training and in what format is it consumed in?
  • If you record webinars, how easy are these to find? Who uses them? Are they useful?
  • Where's the documentation and in what Format is it all in?
  • Do we have localised Content? Different help for different types of Partners.
Most Partner or Channel Management Principles contain a Partner Training Strategy underpinned with a 'Train the Trainer' approach...

...but is this enough in today's fast paced world?

HelpTopic.Name: Upload Additional Help
HelpTopic.Summary: How to upload Help data in bulk from XML files

HelpTopics.HelpTopic:
You can bulk upload Help Content and Helped Page configuration data by proceeding as follows:

  • Create an XML data file: You can use XML to define the Help records you wish to create. Please refer to our support pages for information on the required format;
  • Save your XML file locally.
  • Create a Salesforce Document: "Choose File" and select your XML file to upload;
  • Obtain the "View File" URL of the Document: Click the "View File" link in the Document record and copy the resulting address from your browser.
  • Paste the URL into the text box below.
  • Click the Upsert Documentation button: Note that this will overwrite the relevant help records: we recommend you back up your data prior to any upload.
